title: Adams & Green 1993 reduction of AF slice stiffness with reduced specimen width (size effect)

quantity.name: reduction in stiffness
quantity.definition: % reduction of vertical stiffness vs intact 30 mm slice after vertical cuts that shorten embedded fibre length (fibre-matrix interaction / size effect)

source.sample: 11 vertical lateral-annulus slices (5 mm thick, ~30 mm wide, bone-AF-bone) from 6 cadaveric lumbar spines

protocol.summary: Vertical slices of outer lateral annulus with bone ends potted in dental stone (outer surface not trimmed, lamellae continuous bone to bone); slicing under PEG/0.15 M NaCl spray (no swelling), surfaces covered in Clingfilm; vertical tension to ~70% of estimated UTS with 2.0 s linear ramp load/unload cycles; stiffness = gradient of linear region at 70% EUTS (also 35% EUTS); then sequential vertical cuts (1, 3, 7) reducing effective width 30 -> 15 -> 7.5 -> 3.75 mm.
how_to_simulate: Model the slice with 30, 15, 7.5, 3.75 mm effective widths (cut fibres)
Report % stiffness reduction relative to the 30 mm slice

data.x: 1 cut (15 mm effective width, mean fibre length 9.3 mm), at 70% EUTS

extraction.check_notes: Table 2 from text layer (checked; '25l' read as 251). Mean/SD rows computed by extractor. Donors (M-19, M-40, F-45, M-48, M-51, M-71) also appear in Green 1993 (Part II) - same spines, different (lateral) slices. doi not printed.

pass_rule.rule: |model - mean| <= 1 SD (or inside [min, max] when no SD)
